title: They Stole Your Attention
excerpt: The feed is a slot machine tuned by AI to harvest your focus. Twenty years of logged data on what it took, and what it sells for.
content_html:
Trillion-dollar machines compete for your next 47 seconds. Here are the logs.

> the feed is gacha

> each post a crate

> addictive randomisation

> the ai targets your televised weakness

> it learns while you are unaware

> attention is valuable

> and as you know it's getting mined for revenue

> you work deeply, your mind is outcompeted

> your willpower dies

> the only winning move is not to play

Seconds of attention on one screen before switching

Logged screen focus, knowledge workers & students · Gloria Mark, UC Irvine

202547, reaffirmed (replications 44–50)

Measured by unobtrusive computer logging, workplace and home. The famous “goldfish attention span” stat is folklore; these are logged durations. The 2025 column marks Mark's January 2025 reaffirmation: the average has held at 47 seconds since ~2016, a steady state. Whisker shows the 40–50s band across the median and independent replications.

> UC Irvine has logged screen focus for twenty years

> 2004: two and a half minutes on one screen

> 2012: 75 seconds

> 2016: 47 seconds. median 40.

> 2025: still 47.

> the machine only has to win once every 47 seconds
